1.word_for_word: eka-catvāriṃśake — in the forty-first chapter; purīm prāviśan — entering the city; rajakam — the washerman; tataḥ varān adāt tuṣṭaḥ — then, pleased, bestowed boons; sudāmnaḥ vāyakasya ca — upon Sudāmā and the weaver; sa-śaṅkam akrūra-manaḥ prabodhya — reassuring Akrūra's anxious mind; sva-dhāma-sandarśana-sat-kṛpātaḥ — by the gracious vision of his own divine abode; sva-rāja-dhānīm mathurām apaśyat — he beheld his royal capital Mathurā; alaṅkṛta-ananta-mahotsava-āḍhyām — adorned and rich with innumerable festivities
1.translation: In the forty-first chapter Kṛṣṇa enters the city, deals with the washerman, and later, being pleased, bestows boons upon Sudāmā and the weaver. Having dispelled Akrūra's doubts through the gracious revelation of his own divine abode, Kṛṣṇa beheld Mathurā, his royal capital, richly adorned for innumerable festivities.

4.word_for_word: bhūmau viyati jale vā — on earth, in the sky or in water; yāvanti adbhutāni — whatever wonders there are; tāni tvayi eva santi — all exist in you alone; tam tvām paśyataḥ me — for me who sees you; kim adbhutam adṛṣṭam — what wonder remains unseen?; sarvam dṛṣṭam — everything has been seen
4.translation: Whatever wonders exist on earth, in the sky or in the water are all contained in you alone. For one who has seen you, what wonder could remain unseen? In seeing you, I have seen them all.

5.word_for_word: mat-prāpteḥ pūrvam eva — even before reaching me; vismita-mukhaḥ lakṣitaḥ asi — you were seen with an astonished face; kim api adbhutam dṛṣṭam eva — surely you saw some marvel; yatra tvayi sarvāṇi adbhutāni santi — in you, in whom all wonders exist; anyatra bhūmi-ādau kim adbhutam dṛṣṭam — what wonder could I have seen elsewhere?; tvām vinā na tatra kiñcit adbhutam — apart from you, nothing there is wondrous; brahman — O Supreme Lord
5.translation: Kṛṣṇa could object, ‘Even before you came back to me, your face showed astonishment, so you must have seen some wonder in the earth, sky or water.’ Akrūra answers: ‘All wonders exist in you. Once I see you here, what separate wonder could I have seen elsewhere? Apart from you, nothing there possesses independent wonder.’ ‘Brahman’ is an address meaning ‘O Supreme Lord’; a reading ‘brahma’ is also noted.

6.word_for_word: gāndinī-sutaḥ — son of Gāndinī; akrūraḥ — Akrūra

7.word_for_word: dṛṣṭim na adaduḥ — they did not withdraw their gaze; paśyantaḥ eva sthitāḥ — they remained simply watching
7.translation: The phrase means that they did not take their eyes away; they remained standing there, simply gazing at Kṛṣṇa and Rāma.

8.word_for_word: rāma-kṛṣṇa-āgamanam pratīkṣamāṇāḥ — waiting for Rāma and Kṛṣṇa to come; sthitāḥ — they remained
8.translation: They remained there waiting for the arrival of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa.

10.word_for_word: sva-gṛham ca praviśatām — let the two enter my house; avamucya — alighting, taking off; uttārya — bringing down; viśrāmya — resting
10.translation: The sense is: ‘Please enter my house; alight from the chariot and rest.’

12.word_for_word: sa-agrajaḥ — together with his elder brother; saha gopālaiḥ — together with the cowherd boys
12.translation: ‘With his elder brother’ is to be understood together with the cowherds who accompanied them.

13.word_for_word: yat-śaucena — by whose purifying water; yasya pāda-rajasā kṣālana-udakena — by water that washed the dust from his feet; gṛha-aṅganasthitena — placed within the courtyard of the house
13.translation: The ‘purification’ refers to water that had washed the dust from his feet and was kept in the courtyard of the house.

14.word_for_word: ślokyaḥ — worthy of praise; puṇya-kīrti-arhaḥ — deserving sacred fame; ekānta-bhaktānām yā gatiḥ — the destination attained by exclusive devotees; tām ca lebhe — he attained that as well
14.translation: ‘Ślokya’ means worthy of praise and sacred renown. He also attained the destination reserved for exclusive devotees.

15.word_for_word: apunan — purified; pavitritavatyaḥ — made holy; yābhiḥ adbhiḥ — by those waters; svaḥ svargam prāptāḥ — attained heaven
15.translation: Those waters purified them; through those very waters they attained heaven.

16.word_for_word: prārthayamānaḥ namaskaroti — while making his request, he bows; deva-deva iti — beginning ‘O God of gods’; ataḥ param anyat śreyaḥ na asti — there is no greater good beyond this; bahudhā sambodhayati — therefore he addresses the Lord in many ways
16.translation: As he makes his request he bows down, beginning with ‘O God of gods.’ Believing that no higher good exists beyond obtaining the Lord, he addresses him with many exalted names.

17.word_for_word: yadu-cakrāya druhyati iti yadu-cakra-dhruk — one who is hostile to the circle of Yadus; tam kaṃsam hatvā — after killing that Kaṃsa; suhṛdām priyam vitariṣye — I shall bestow what is dear to our friends
17.translation: ‘The enemy of the Yadu circle’ means Kaṃsa, who is hostile to the Yadus. ‘After killing him, I shall bestow upon our friends what is dear to them.’

18.word_for_word: rāma-kṛṣṇau ānītau iti — ‘Rāma and Kṛṣṇa have been brought’; sva-kṛtam karma āvedya — reporting the task he himself had accomplished; samarpya — handing the matter over
18.translation: Akrūra reports the task he had been assigned—‘Rāma and Kṛṣṇa have been brought’—and thereby formally hands over the result of his mission.

19.word_for_word: gopaiḥ parivāritaḥ — surrounded by the cowherds; prāviśat — he entered
19.translation: Kṛṣṇa entered the city surrounded by the cowherds.

20.word_for_word: śrī-kṛṣṇa-dṛṣṭām purīm anuvarṇayati caturbhiḥ — four verses describe the city seen by Kṛṣṇa; sphāṭikāni tuṅgāni gopurāṇi — lofty crystal gateways; pura-dvārāṇi gṛha-dvārāṇi ca — city gates and house gates; bṛhanti hema-mayāni kapāṭāni toraṇāni ca — great golden doors and arches; tāmram ca āraḥ ārakūṭaḥ — copper and brass; tan-mayāḥ koṣṭhāḥ dhānya-agāra-aśva-śālā-ādayaḥ — storerooms, granaries, stables and the like made from them; parikhābhiḥ durāsadām — difficult to approach because of surrounding moats; udyānaiḥ upavanaiḥ ca upaśobhitām — adorned with distant gardens and nearby groves
20.translation: Four verses describe Mathurā as Kṛṣṇa saw it. It had lofty crystal gateways at the city entrances and houses, massive golden doors and arches, and buildings such as storerooms, granaries and stables made or faced with copper and brass. Defensive moats dug around it made the city difficult to approach, while distant gardens and nearby pleasure groves beautified it.

21.word_for_word: sauvarṇāḥ śṛṅgāṭakāḥ catuṣpathāḥ — golden crossroads and four-way intersections; harmyāṇi — mansions; dhaninām gṛhāṇi — houses of the wealthy; niṣkuṭāḥ — domestic pleasure gardens; śreṇīnām sabhābhiḥ — assembly places of artisan guilds; amālāḥ sphaṭikāḥ — spotless crystals; haritaḥ marakatāḥ — green emeralds; vaidūrya-ādi-ratnaiḥ juṣṭeṣu valabhī-ādiṣu — balconies and structures set with vaidūrya and other gems; pārāvataiḥ barhibhiḥ ca nāditām — resounding with pigeons and peacocks; valabhyaḥ — curved roofed projections over house fronts; vedayaḥ — raised platforms below them; jālamukha-randhrāṇi — lattice-window openings; gavākṣa-chidrāṇi — window apertures; kuṭṭimāni — gem-inlaid floors; rathyāḥ — royal roads; āpaṇāḥ — market streets; catvarāṇi — courtyards or squares; saṃsiktāni — sprinkled; prakīrṇa-mālya-ādīni — strewn with garlands and the like
21.translation: The city had golden crossroads, mansions and houses of the wealthy with their domestic gardens, guild halls where craftsmen gathered, and many other buildings. Spotless crystal, green emerald and vaidūrya and other jewels adorned balconies and architectural projections where pigeons and peacocks called. Śrīdhara explains the valabhīs as curved roofed projections at house fronts, with platforms below them, lattice openings and windows; the floors were inlaid with gems. Royal roads, market streets, smaller roads and open squares had all been sprinkled with water and strewn with garlands and other decorations.

23.word_for_word: su-alaṅkṛtāni dvārāṇi yeṣām gṛhāḥ — houses whose doorways were beautifully decorated; āpūrṇaiḥ kumbhaiḥ — with full water-pots; dadhnā candanena ca ukṣitaiḥ — sprinkled with yogurt and sandal paste; prasūnānām dīpānām ca āvalayaḥ — rows of flowers and lamps; rambhāḥ kramukāḥ — banana and betel-nut trees; phala-gucchaiḥ upalakṣitāḥ — marked by clusters of fruit; sa-ketubhiḥ — with banners and flags; paṭṭikā — bands of fine cloth; dvāreṣu ubhayataḥ taṇḍulānām upari kumbhāḥ — pots set on rice at both sides of each doorway; tat-paritaḥ prasūna-āvalayaḥ — rings of flowers around them; kaṇṭhe paṭṭikā — cloth bands around their necks; mukhe cūta-ādi-pallavāḥ — mango and other leaves at the mouth; tad-upari pātra-antare dīpa-āvalayaḥ — rows of lamps above in separate vessels
23.translation: The houses had richly decorated entrances: full ceremonial pots sprinkled with yogurt and sandalwood, rows of flowers and lamps, banana and betel-nut trees bearing clusters of fruit, flags, banners and strips of fine cloth. Śrīdhara explains the custom in detail: at each side of a doorway a pot was set upon rice, surrounded with flowers, tied at the neck with a strip of cloth, filled at the mouth with mango and other fresh leaves, with lamps arranged above or nearby; banana plants, betel-nut trees, flags and arches completed the decoration.

24.word_for_word: nara-deva-vartmanā — by the king's road; rāja-mārgeṇa — along the royal highway; tām purīm saṃpraviṣṭau — the two entered that city
24.translation: The two brothers entered Mathurā along the royal road.

25.word_for_word: autsukyam āha dvayena — two verses describe the women's eagerness; viparyak viparītam dhṛtāni vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni ca yābhiḥ — some put garments and ornaments on incorrectly or reversed; yugaleṣu kuṇḍala-kaṅkaṇa-ādiṣu ekam vismṛtya — forgetting one item of a matching pair, such as an earring or bracelet; ekam eva patrakam śravaṇe — only one ear ornament; ekam eva nūpuram — only one anklet; na aṅktvā — without completing cosmetic application; ekasmin eva locane añjanam nidhāya — putting collyrium in only one eye
25.translation: Two verses describe the women's eagerness to see Kṛṣṇa. Some put on garments and ornaments backwards or incorrectly; others forgot one item from paired ornaments such as earrings or bracelets, wearing only one earring or one anklet. Some rushed out before finishing their cosmetics, with collyrium applied to only one eye.

26.word_for_word: tad bhojanam tyaktvā — abandoning their meal; abhajyamānāḥ — while being massaged; sakhībhiḥ kriyamāṇa-taila-abhyaṅgāḥ — friends applying oil to them; akṛta-upamajjanāḥ — before washing; akṛta-snānaḥ — before bathing; arbham — a child; apohya — setting aside, removing
26.translation: Some abandoned their meal; some ran out while friends were still applying oil to their bodies, before washing or bathing; others even set aside the child they were tending.

27.word_for_word: pragalbhāḥ līlāḥ — confident, expressive playful gestures; tābhiḥ hasitāni nirīkṣaṇāni ca — smiles and glances arising from them; śriyam ramayati iti śrī-ramaṇaḥ — he who delights Śrī; tena ātmanā vapuṣā — with that very body; tāsām dṛśām utsavam dadan — giving a festival to their eyes; manāṃsi jahāra — stole their minds
27.translation: Through his confident and graceful playful gestures, smiles and glances, Kṛṣṇa—he who delights Śrī—made his own form a festival for the women's eyes and stole their minds.

28.word_for_word: muhuḥ śrutatvāt tad-gata-cetasaḥ — because they had heard about him repeatedly, their minds were already absorbed in him; sadyaḥ tam dṛṣṭvā — seeing him directly at once; tasya prekṣaṇam ca utsmitam ca tad eva sudhā — his glance and smile themselves were nectar; sudhā-tayoḥ ukṣaṇam secanam — sprinkling with that nectar; tena labdhaḥ mānaḥ yābhiḥ — thereby honored; dṛśā udghāṭitena netra-dvāreṇa — through the eye as an opened doorway; ātmani manasi labdham — received into the mind; pariṣvajya — embracing him there; tad-aprāpti-janitam anantam ādhim jahuḥ — they gave up endless mental pain caused by not attaining him; he arindama — O subduer of enemies; nirjita-kāma — conqueror of desire
28.translation: Because they had repeatedly heard about Kṛṣṇa, their minds were already fixed on him. Now, seeing him directly, they received the nectar of his glance and smile as though sprinkled with it. Through the opened doorway of their eyes they brought him into the mind and embraced him there, abandoning the long mental anguish born from not having seen him. Śrīdhara notes the address ‘O subduer of enemies’ as ‘conqueror of desire,’ warning the hearer not to mistake this description for ordinary erotic absorption.

29.word_for_word: saumanasyaiḥ — with flowers, or with auspicious joyful states of mind; kusuma-samūhaiḥ — groups of flowers; śobhana-mano-bhāvaiḥ vā — alternatively, beautiful mental sentiments
29.translation: ‘Saumanasya’ may mean clusters of flowers or, alternatively, beautiful and auspicious states of mind.

31.word_for_word: paurāḥ — inhabitants of the city; pura-striyaḥ — specifically the women of the city
31.translation: ‘Pauras’ here refers specifically to the women of the city.

32.word_for_word: rajakaḥ — washerman; vastra-nirṇejakaḥ — one who cleans garments; sa eva vastrāṇām raṅgam api kurvan — the same man also dyed garments; raṅga-kāraḥ — dyer
32.translation: The rajaka was a washerman who cleaned garments; he also dyed them and thus functioned as a dyer.

35.word_for_word: he udvṛttāḥ — O arrogant ones; girau vane caratha ye nityam — you who always wander on mountain and in forest; te yūyam pūrvam paridhatta — ‘you should wear such garments’ used in the sense of an improbable supposition; sambhāvanāyām loṭ — imperative expressing conjecture; abhīpsatha — you desire; prārthayadhvam — you ask for
35.translation: The washerman addresses them as ‘arrogant fellows who are accustomed to wandering in mountains and forests.’ The imperative in ‘wear such garments’ is used with a scornful hypothetical force: ‘Do you imagine that people like you are fit to wear them?’ ‘Abhīpsatha’ means ‘you desire’ or ‘you ask for.’

36.word_for_word: rāja-kulāni — royal establishments; rājakīyāḥ — officers of the king; lumpanti — plunder; niḥsvam kurvanti — strip a person of possessions
36.translation: The reference is to the king's officers, who would seize a transgressor's property and reduce him to poverty.

38.word_for_word: vāsaḥ-kośān — bundles or stores of garments; vastra-puṭakān — packets of clothing
38.translation: ‘Vāsaḥ-kośa’ means bundles or packets of clothing.

40.word_for_word: vāyakaḥ — weaver; tantu-vāya-viśeṣaḥ — a particular kind of textile worker; veṣam — attire, adornment; caileyaiḥ — made of cloth; vastra-mayaiḥ akalpaiḥ bhūṣaṇaiḥ — ornaments fashioned from fabric
40.translation: The vāyaka is a weaver or specialist textile-worker. ‘Veṣa’ means attire or adornment, and the ‘akalpas’ were decorative ornaments made from cloth.

41.word_for_word: parvaṇi — on a festive occasion; utsave — at a festival
41.translation: ‘Parvan’ here means a festival or festive occasion.

42.word_for_word: iha loke — in this world; paramām śriyam — supreme prosperity; balam — strength; aiśvaryam — lordly power; indriyam — sensory capacity; tat-pāṭavam — excellence and acuity of the senses; prādāt — he bestowed
42.translation: In this very world Kṛṣṇa bestowed upon him supreme prosperity, strength, power and exceptional acuity of the senses.

46.word_for_word: kṣemāya — for security; abhayāya — for fearlessness; bhavāya — for becoming; udbhavāya — for flourishing or arising
46.translation: ‘Kṣema’ means security or freedom from fear; ‘bhava’ here means flourishing or coming into well-being.

47.word_for_word: rajaka-vadhena vāyaka-anugraheṇa ca — by killing the washerman and favoring the weaver; viṣama-dṛṣṭitayā anīśvaratā na āśaṅkanīyā — one should not suspect partiality and therefore lack of true lordship; samayoḥ — because the two Lords are impartial; suhṛdoḥ — because they are well-wishers; jagad-ātmanoḥ — because they are the Self of the universe
47.translation: One should not infer from the killing of the washerman and the blessing of the weaver that Rāma and Kṛṣṇa are partial and therefore not truly divine. The verse itself gives the reason: they are impartial, they are the well-wishers of all, and they are the very Self of the universe.

49.word_for_word: iti abhipretya — understanding this intention; iti evam vijñāpayan — making his request in this manner; tat-matam jñātvā — knowing what they desired
49.translation: The phrase means that, having expressed his request in this manner, he understood their intention and acted in accordance with what they desired.

52.word_for_word: anvaya-vardhinīm — increasing the lineage; vaṃśe vṛddhi-matīm — bringing growth to the family line; aprārthitam śrī-prabhṛtikam ca dattvā — also granting unasked-for blessings beginning with prosperity; tataḥ nirjagāma — then he departed
52.translation: The blessing ‘anvaya-vardhinī’ means one that increases and causes the family lineage to flourish. Kṛṣṇa also granted prosperity and other blessings that had not even been requested, and then departed.
